brief.greeting: Good morning. GPT‑6 got a user manual while Anthropic throws cash at engineers.

stories.headline: OpenAI publishes GPT‑6 selection guide
stories.body: **Quick start for GPT‑6:** OpenAI’s blog walks startups through picking a GPT‑6 variant, tweaking reasoning effort, prompt engineering, tool integration, and production pipelines.
stories.why: Helps you cut trial‑and‑error when deploying next‑gen LLMs.

stories.headline: Anthropic pours $100 M into engineer training
stories.body: **Big bet on people:** Anthropic announced a $100 million fund to upskill 10,000 engineers, aiming to close the enterprise AI talent gap.
stories.why: More trained engineers means faster adoption of advanced AI tools in production.

stories.headline: Friday security patches hit major Linux distros
stories.body: **Patch rush:** LWN reports updates for kernel, OpenSSH, and Firefox across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, and SUSE.
stories.why: Keeps your servers and devices safe without a reboot nightmare.

quick_hits.text: **Local LLM:** ds4 lets you run large models on‑premise, from Redis creator.
**Fast reports:** Hugging Face open‑sources AstaBrief, a speedy report‑generation model.
**Test suite:** Linux Test Project ships September 2026 release with 382 patches.
**Functional TS:** Effect‑TS/effect climbs trending, offers FP patterns for production apps.
**Retro hack:** 68k‑MBC builds a 68008 computer from just three ICs.

highlights.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family
highlights.summary: OpenAI blog outlines how startups can select GPT-6 models, adjust reasoning effort, refine prompts, integrate tools, and set up production workflows.
highlights.detail: The guide covers practical steps for model selection, prompt engineering, and tool coordination, aiming to help early-stage companies adopt GPT-6 efficiently. It also discusses cost‑performance trade‑offs and deployment considerations.

highlights.title: From the creator of Redis; run LLM locally with ds4
highlights.summary: A Hacker News post highlights ds4, a tool from the creator of Redis for running large language models locally.
highlights.detail: The announcement emphasizes ease of setup and low‑resource operation, positioning ds4 as an alternative to cloud‑based inference. It targets developers who need offline model execution.

highlights.title: Greg Kroah-Hartman – Security in the LLM Age [video]
highlights.summary: A Hacker News video features Greg Kroah-Hartman discussing security challenges in the era of large language models.
highlights.detail: The talk reviews potential attack vectors introduced by LLM integration, such as prompt injection and model poisoning, and suggests mitigation strategies for open‑source projects.

highlights.title: Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap
highlights.summary: Anthropic announced a $100 million investment to train 10,000 engineers and address the enterprise AI talent shortage.
highlights.detail: The program will provide curriculum, mentorship, and hands‑on projects using Anthropic’s models, aiming to build a pipeline of skilled AI professionals for corporate adoption.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Friday security updates were released for multiple Linux distributions, covering packages such as kernel, openssh, and firefox across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, and SUSE.
highlights.detail: Each distro’s update addresses CVEs relevant to the listed components, with patched versions pushed to official repositories. Administrators should apply them promptly to maintain system integrity. The announcement aggregates many upstream fixes into a single bulletin.

items.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
items.summary: Hugging Face blog reports the open‑source release of AstaBrief, a fast report‑generation model from the Asta suite.
items.detail: AstaBrief is optimized for low‑latency summarization of structured data, and the repository includes pretrained weights, inference scripts, and integration examples.

items.title: Model: Cloudflare/clef-flash
items.summary: The Cloudflare/clef-flash model on Hugging Face has received 1,303 downloads and 289 likes.
items.detail: Clef-flash is an image‑text‑to‑text transformer designed for rapid multimodal inference, and its popularity reflects growing interest in lightweight vision‑language models.

items.title: Model: orcarouter/OrcaSAQ-2-Cyber-27B-Uncensored-GGUF
items.summary: OrcaSAQ-2-Cyber-27B-Uncensored model on Hugging Face has 9,533 downloads and 278 likes.
items.detail: The model is provided in GGUF format for efficient inference on consumer hardware. It targets uncensored question‑answering tasks and follows the OrcaSAQ series lineage. No licensing details were included in the brief listing.

items.title: Security updates for Friday
items.summary: Friday security updates were released for multiple Linux distributions, covering packages such as kernel, openssh, and firefox across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, and SUSE.
items.detail: Each distro’s update addresses CVEs relevant to the listed components, with patched versions pushed to official repositories. Administrators should apply them promptly to maintain system integrity. The announcement aggregates many upstream fixes into a single bulletin.

items.title: Linux Test Project suite stable release for September 2026
items.summary: The Linux Test Project released its stable September 2026 version, incorporating 382 patches from 41 authors since the May 2026 release.
items.detail: The update adds new test cases and refines existing ones to improve kernel compliance verification. It continues the project’s regular cadence of quarterly releases, reflecting ongoing community contributions. Detailed changelog is available in the announcement.

items.title: [$] Beyond the &
items.summary: At RustConf 2026, language team lead Tyler Mandry announced efforts to make user‑defined smart pointers as flexible as built‑in references.
items.detail: The proposal targets limitations where smart pointers cannot emulate certain reference operations, aiming to reduce boilerplate and improve ergonomics. Implementation will require changes to the borrow checker and library traits, with a timeline extending into the next Rust edition.

items.title: 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge: A Homebrew Computer In Only Three ICs
items.summary: The 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge entry '68k‑MBC' is a hole‑through‑board 68008 computer built using only three integrated circuits.
items.detail: The design leverages a minimal component count to demonstrate functional computing with a 68k core, fitting entirely on a single perfboard. It showcases how classic architectures can be realized with modern, readily available ICs.

items.title: 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge: Lunar Lander on the PDP-1
items.summary: The 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge features a Lunar Lander implementation running on a PDP‑1 replica.
items.detail: The project recreates the classic text‑based game on hardware emulating the 1960s PDP‑1, highlighting the system’s original instruction set and timing constraints. It serves both as a nostalgic demo and a teaching tool for early computer architecture.

items.title: Electronic Busy Board is Fun for Kids and Hackers
items.summary: Hackaday describes a DIY electronic busy board, a tactile toy featuring assorted buttons, switches, and sensors that can be assembled for kids and hobbyists.
items.detail: The article explains how the board can be built from inexpensive components and repurposed for learning electronics or as a debugging aid for developers. It includes wiring diagrams and suggestions for expanding functionality with microcontrollers.

items.title: Effect-TS/effect
items.summary: Effect-TS/effect is a TypeScript library aimed at building production‑ready applications with functional programming patterns.
items.detail: The repository provides abstractions for effect management, error handling, and resource safety, targeting Node.js and browser environments. It integrates with existing TypeScript tooling and emphasizes type‑safe APIs.

items.title: ayghri/i-have-adhd
items.summary: ayghri/i-have-adhd is a Python project that modifies a coding agent's output to be more concise and ADHD‑friendly.
items.detail: The tool filters or reformats responses to reduce verbosity, aiming to keep attention focused. It can be integrated into automated coding assistants to improve usability for neurodiverse users.

items.title: cloudflare/workerd
items.summary: cloudflare/workerd is the C++ runtime that executes JavaScript and WebAssembly for Cloudflare Workers.
items.detail: The project implements the V8 engine and a lightweight sandbox, enabling fast edge computing. It supports the Workers API and can be used locally for development and testing.

items.title: coreyhaines31/marketingskills
items.summary: coreyhaines31/marketingskills offers prompt templates and utilities for Claude Code and AI agents to perform marketing tasks such as copywriting and SEO.
items.detail: The repository bundles prompts, example workflows, and evaluation scripts to help AI agents generate conversion‑focused content. It targets developers building AI‑driven marketing automation.

items.title: cursor/plugins
items.summary: cursor/plugins defines the specification for Cursor editor plugins and includes a set of official plugins.
items.detail: The spec outlines how plugins can extend the editor with new commands, UI elements, and language support. Official plugins demonstrate integrations such as code linting, AI assistance, and custom keybindings.

items.title: firebase/firebase-ios-sdk
items.summary: Firebase SDK for Apple app development, hosted on GitHub and currently trending in the C++ category.
items.detail: The repository offers a collection of libraries enabling iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS apps to integrate Firebase services such as analytics, authentication, cloud messaging, and remote config. It is maintained by Google and follows Apple's development guidelines. The SDK is written primarily in Objective‑C and Swift, with some C++ components for cross‑platform support.
